chunks: You will be tried with your wealth and yourselves, and you will hear much annoyance from those who were given the Book before you and from the polytheists. And if you are patient and fear Allah, then indeed that is of the matters requiring resolve.

key_terms.الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ: Those who were given the Book (People of the Book)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific trials and sources of annoyance mentioned for believers in Surah Aal-Imran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the trials of the Ahl al-Bayt and the Imams, illustrating that enduring hardship from both monotheistic communities (People of the Book) and polytheists is a hallmark of steadfastness. The emphasis on 'azm al-umur' (firm resolve) highlights that true piety is tested not just in isolation, but through public scrutiny and material loss, reinforcing the concept of 'Sabr al-Jamil' (beautiful patience) as a divine virtue.
